Let's clarify the relationship.
A code $C$ is a covering code if $\bigcup_{c \in C} B(c, 1) = \{0,1,2\}^n$.
A code $C$ is *minimal* if no proper subset of $C$ is a covering code.
If two codewords $c_1, c_2 \in C$ have distance $d(c_1, c_2) \le 2$, then $B(c_1, 1) \cap B(c_2, 1) \neq \emptyset$. In fact, if $d(c_1, c_2)=1$, $c_1 \in B(c_2, 1)$ and $c_2 \in B(c_1, 1)$. If $d(c_1, c_2)=2$, they share a common neighbor.
However, having overlapping balls doesn't necessarily mean one is redundant. Redundancy means $B(c_1, 1) \subseteq \bigcup_{c \in C \setminus \{c_1\}} B(c, 1)$.
